Russophobia (the fear or hatred of Russia or Russians)
A systematic disrespect, or even disdain towards the Russian people and culture, particularly if at the hands of the country's political and cultural elite.

ety.text: From English Russophobia. While the broader sense "fear/hatred of Russians" has existed since at least 1879, the term was popularized in the late 1980s by the Russian mathematician and writer Igor Shafarevich in the 2nd sense; partly intended as a counter to those who systematically denounced perceived antisemitism in the USSR, but not other types of racism and persecution as the country was collapsing, an attitude he found hypocritical. Can be analysed as ру́сский (rússkij, “ethnic Russian people”) + -о- (-o-) + фо́бия (fóbija, “phobia, fear or hatred of”).
